about: M3: the M1 scenes said in other words (30 lines). After each line the scene (diagram.extract.scene_key) must equal the reference fixture's after its line of the same number. Answers for the lines the fast path leaves unread: m3_llm_answers.json (recorded live by tools/record_m3.py).

lines: Picture a crate resting on a ramp inclined at 30 degrees.
The crate has a mass of five kilograms.
Someone pushes it up the ramp with a force of 5 newtons.
Let the friction coefficient be 0.3.
Let's raise the angle to 45 degrees.
Consider a heavy block lying on the ground.
Its mass is 10 kg and a 20 newton push acts on it.
Take mu equal to 0.5.
Increase the push to 60 newtons.
Think of a 10 kg block on the floor.
Mu static is 0.5 while mu kinetic is 0.4.
A force of 45 newtons pushes it to the right.
The push becomes 55 newtons.
Imagine block A on block B on the floor.
A 50 newton force pulls block B.
Block A is 2 kg and block B is 3 kg.
Between A and B the friction coefficient is 0.4.
There is no friction with the floor.
Imagine two masses connected by a string over a pulley.
The masses are 2 kg and 3 kg.
Consider a mass suspended from a spring.
The spring's stiffness is 100 newtons per metre and the mass weighs 0.5 kg.
Imagine a block on a table tied with a string that goes over a pulley to a mass hanging down.
The table block is 4 kg and the one hanging is 1 kg.
The table has no friction.
Now take the friction coefficient as 0.2.
Change mu to 0.3.
Suppose we stack two blocks on the floor.
The upper block is 2 kg and the lower one is 3 kg.
We push the lower block with 10 newtons.
